title: A Christmas Carol
blurb: A Christmas Carol. In Prose. Being a Ghost Story of Christmas, commonly known as A Christmas Carol, is a novella by Charles Dickens, first published in London by Chapman & Hall in 1843 and illustrated by John Leech.

title: A Confederacy of Dunces

title: A Tale of Two Cities
blurb: A Tale of Two Cities is a historical novel published in 1859 by English author Charles Dickens, set in London and Paris before and during the French Revolution.

title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
blurb: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland is an 1865 English children's novel by Lewis Carroll. It tells the story of a little girl named Alice who falls through a rabbit hole into a fantasy world of anthropomorphic creatures. It is seen as an example of the literary nonsense genre.

title: All the Light We Cannot See
blurb: All the Light We Cannot See is a 2014 war novel by American author Anthony Doerr. The novel is set during World War II.

title: And Then There Were None

title: Anna Karenina
blurb: Anna Karenina is a novel, first published in book form in 1878, by the Russian author Leo Tolstoy. Often considered to be among the greatest works of world literature, Tolstoy himself called it his first true novel.

title: Anne of Green Gables
blurb: Anne of Green Gables is a 1908 novel by the Canadian author Lucy Maud Montgomery. Written for all ages, it has been considered a classic children's novel since the mid-20th century.

title: Atlas
blurb: A bound collection of maps, for planning journeys or just wandering with a finger.

title: Blood Meridian

title: Brave New World
blurb: Brave New World is a dystopian novel by English author Aldous Huxley, written in 1931, and published in 1932.

title: Carmilla

title: Carrie

title: Cookbook
blurb: A collection of recipes, often splattered and annotated by the people who cook from it.

title: Coraline

title: Crime and Punishment

title: Demon Copperhead

title: Discworld
blurb: Discworld is a collection of fantasy comedy novels, graphic novels, short stories, and associated works conceived and primarily written by the English author Terry Pratchett.

title: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?

title: Don Quixote
blurb: Don Quixote is a novel by Miguel de Cervantes, written in Early Modern Spanish and published in two parts in 1605 and 1615.

title: Dracula

title: Dune
blurb: Frank Herbert's 1965 epic of a desert planet, its giant sandworms and the spice everyone wants.

title: East of Eden

title: Fahrenheit 451

blurb: Mary Shelley's 1818 novel of a scientist who builds a living creature and then abandons it.

title: Graphic novel
blurb: A book-length story told in comics, from memoirs to superheroes.

title: Guinness World Records
blurb: Guinness World Records, known from its inception in 1955 until 1999 as The Guinness Book of Records and in previous United States editions as The Guinness Book of World Records, is a British reference book published annually, listing world records both of human achievements and the extremes of the…

blurb: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone is a fantasy novel by British author J. K. Rowling. It is the first novel in the Harry Potter series and was Rowling's debut novel.

title: Illuminated manuscript

blurb: Invisible Man is Ralph Ellison's first novel, and the only one published during his lifetime. title: Jane Eyre

title: Klara and the Sun

title: Lord of the Flies
blurb: Lord of the Flies is the 1954 debut novel of British author William Golding. The plot concerns a group of prepubescent British boys who are stranded on an uninhabited island and their disastrous attempts to govern themselves that lead to a descent into savagery.

title: Macbeth

title: Midnight's Children

blurb: A snowbound train, a dead passenger and Hercule Poirot, in Agatha Christie's 1934 mystery.

title: Olive Kitteridge

title: One Thousand and One Nights
blurb: One Thousand and One Nights or The Thousand and One Nights is a collection of Middle Eastern folktales compiled in the Arabic language during the Islamic Golden Age.

title: Pop-up book

title: Pride and Prejudice
blurb: Jane Austen's 1813 comedy of manners, in which Elizabeth Bennet and Mr Darcy misjudge each other at length.

blurb: Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde is an 1886 Gothic horror novella by Scottish author Robert Louis Stevenson.

title: The Caine Mutiny

title: The Cat in the Hat

title: The Dresden Files

blurb: The God of Small Things is the 1997 debut novel written by Indian author Arundhati Roy. title: The Great Gatsby
blurb: Parties, longing and a green light across the bay: Fitzgerald's portrait of the Jazz Age.

title: The Hobbit

title: The Little Prince
blurb: A pilot stranded in the desert meets a small boy from an asteroid, in a fable for grown-ups.

title: The Lord of the Rings

title: The Love Hypothesis

title: The Lovely Bones

title: The Magician's Nephew
blurb: The Magician's Nephew is a portal fantasy novel by British author C. S. Lewis, published in 1955 by The Bodley Head. It is the sixth published of seven novels in The Chronicles of Narnia.

title: The Man in the High Castle
blurb: The Man in the High Castle is an alternative history novel by Philip K. Dick, first published in 1962, which imagines a world in which the Axis powers won World War II.

title: The Metamorphosis
blurb: The Metamorphosis, also translated as The Transformation, is a novella by Franz Kafka published in 1915.

title: The Midnight Library

title: The Overstory
blurb: The Overstory is a novel by American author Richard Powers, published in 2018 by W. W. Norton & Company. The book follows nine Americans whose unique life experiences with trees bring them together to address the destruction of forests.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
blurb: The Picture of Dorian Gray is an 1890 philosophical fiction and Gothic horror novel by Irish author Oscar Wilde.

title: The Shining
blurb: The Shining is a 1977 horror novel by American author Stephen King. It is King's third published novel and first hardcover bestseller; its success firmly established King as a preeminent author in the horror genre.

title: The Stand
blurb: The Stand is an epic post-apocalyptic dark fantasy novel written by American author Stephen King and first published in 1978 by Doubleday.

title: The Stranger

title: The Tempest

title: The Three-Body Problem

title: The Trial
blurb: The Trial is a German-language novel written by the Czech-Jewish writer Franz Kafka in 1914 and 1915 and published posthumously on 26 April 1925.

title: The Very Hungry Caterpillar
blurb: Eric Carle's picture book, holes and all, about a caterpillar eating through a week of food.

title: The Winds of Winter
blurb: The Winds of Winter is the planned sixth and penultimate novel of the epic fantasy series A Song of Ice and Fire by American writer George R. R. Martin. The novel, which has been in the works since 2011, has been described as one of the most anticipated books in modern history.

title: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
blurb: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz is a 1900 children's fantasy novel written by the American author L. Frank Baum and illustrated by W. W. Denslow. It is the first novel in the Oz series of books.

title: There Is No Antimemetics Division
blurb: There Is No Antimemetics Division is a literary work of science fiction–horror by British author qntm.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
blurb: To Kill a Mockingbird is a 1960 Southern Gothic novel by American author Harper Lee. It became instantly successful after its release; in the United States, it is widely read in high schools and middle schools.

title: Treasure Island

title: Ulysses

title: Verity
blurb: Verity is a 2018 psychological romantic thriller novel by American author Colleen Hoover. The narrative follows Lowen Ashleigh, a writer who is hired to complete a bestselling book series after an accident leaves its original author, Verity Crawford, unable to do so.

title: War and Peace
blurb: War and Peace is an epic novel by the Russian author Leo Tolstoy. Set during the Napoleonic Wars, the work comprises both a fictional narrative and chapters in which Tolstoy discusses history and philosophy.

title: Wildwood
blurb: Wildwood is a 2011 fantasy novel by Colin Meloy, illustrated by his wife Carson Ellis. Inspired by classic fantasy novels and folk tales, the book is about two seventh-graders who are drawn into a hidden, magical forest, while trying to rescue a baby kidnapped by crows.

title: Wildwood Imperium
blurb: Wildwood Imperium: The Wildwood Chronicles, Book Three is a 2014 children's fantasy novel by The Decemberists' singer-songwriter Colin Meloy, illustrated by his wife Carson Ellis.

title: Wolf Hall
blurb: Wolf Hall is a 2009 historical novel by English author Hilary Mantel, published by Fourth Estate, named after the Seymour family's seat of Wolfhall, or Wulfhall, in Wiltshire.

title: Wuthering Heights
blurb: Wuthering Heights is the only novel by the English author Emily Brontë, initially published in 1847 under her pen name Ellis Bell.
